newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas climb halts ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas climb halts ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices ended their week-long rally Friday by losing about two cents ahead of the weekend and a gradual relief from 100-degree F heat in the Midwest and parts of Texas, market sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, physical prices slipped an average of two cents to about $2.22 per mmBtu at Henry Hub.
In south Texas, prices similarly fell two cents to about $2.14-2.17 as a gradual cooldown was expected in Dallas to the high-90s F by Monday.
In the Permian Basin market, prices slid sn average of six cents to about $2.15, though deals were reported done as high as $2.17 early and as low as $2.06 late.
Early August deals in the Permian Basin were reported done at $2.02-2.03, which was fairly even with July indices.
Southern California border prices for the weekend also lost several cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s.
San Juan prices slumped to around $2.07-2.11.
In the Midwest, prices lost about two cents to $2.13-2.14 but still held about a two-cent premium to week-ago levels. Chicago city-gate gas similarly eased to around $2.29-2.30.
In the East, swing gas at the New York city gate prices were also quoted a bit softer at $2.40 as cooler weather was expected to follow a brief hot spell in the East.
